function: Allocation of detected spectrum holes (sub-channels) to requesting UAVs by DQN/DDQN, fed by FL-trained CNN wideband spectrum-hole detection from I/Q samples (p. 1, p. 10, p. 15).
system: 3 LTE BSs, 3 UAVs at 90 m (secondary users); 10 MHz band at 1980 MHz, 16 sub-channels; antenna configuration not stated; no RIS (p. 11, Table 1).
method: 1D-CNN multi-label classifier, supervised, trained by federated learning (proposed pwFedAvg, digital aggregation at server); DQN, DDQN and DDQN-soft reinforcement learning for allocation (p. 7-8, p. 10).
data_channel: Synthetic I/Q: MATLAB LTE Toolbox waveforms through site-specific MATLAB ray tracing (OpenStreetMap, Kansas City); binary Markov sub-channel occupancy; one dataset split for training and testing (p. 11-13).
test_conditions: 70/30 train-test split at the same three UAV locations, SNR -10 to 20 dB; local model also tested at other locations; RL with one or two UAVs (p. 12-16).
baselines: Learned only: centralized and local learning, FedAvg [48], with/without fusion; vanilla DQN and DDQN versus DDQN-soft for allocation. No non-learned baseline (p. 13-16).
metrics: Micro-averaged precision, recall and F1-score of spectrum-hole detection; average aggregated utility (kb/s) of the RL allocation versus training episodes (p. 13, p. 15-16).
complexity: none; only qualitative remarks and the 65,537 x 17 Q-table size of tabular Q-learning, which is not adopted (p. 7, p. 10).
openness: none; dataset and source code only promised for future public release, without link (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 11: "We utilize MATLAB’s ray tracer to emulate the wireless channel"; the authors' own site-specific ray tracing (OpenStreetMap, Kansas City), not 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data, and not released.
q2_support: p. 15: "our current results do not address such scenarios"; the FL model is tested on a 30% split at the same three UAV locations (p. 13) and the DDQN only in training (p. 16, Fig. 15); only the local-learning comparison model is tested at other locations (p. 13).
q3_support: p. 13: "the FedAvg algorithm [48] as a baseline alongside our proposed pwFedAvg"; p. 16: "Q-learning methods for resource allocation to a single UAV." Learned baselines only (FedAvg, DQN, DDQN); no non-learned method (energy detection, random or greedy allocation) is compared.
q4_support: p. 7: "which significantly decreases computational complexity" is qualitative; p. 10: "complexity of tabular Q-learning becomes cumbersome." gives only the Q-table size of tabular Q-learning, not adopted; no order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime of the CNN or DDQN.
q5_support: p. 12: "which will be publicly released along with all source codes."; a promise without link or DOI, and the data are the authors' own synthetic dataset, not public or measured.
notes: Borderline eligibility. The main learned contribution is a CNN for wideband spectrum sensing trained by federated learning with pwFedAvg, aggregated digitally at the server (p. 8, Algorithm 1): spectrum sensing is an excluded function and digital FL is outside area 7. Included because the framework also learns the allocation of detected spectrum holes (sub-channels) to the UAVs with DQN/DDQN (p. 10; p. 15: "for allocating spectrum resources to the UAVs"), read as learned resource allocation in aerial links, which Step 1 counts as physical layer, hence area 6. If the reviewer reads this allocation as scheduling or dynamic spectrum access above the physical layer, the decision becomes exclude, reason function (p. 5: the DNN takes raw I/Q samples and outputs the predicted spectrum occupancy vector). q1: the channel is the authors' own site-specific MATLAB ray tracing over OpenStreetMap (Kansas City, 1980 MHz), neither a listed model nor a released public dataset; the reviewer may confirm. q2: Fig. 14 (p. 15) tests the local-learning model of location 1 at locations 2 and 3, but that is a comparison configuration, not the proposed FL model or the DDQN; the paper defers generalization to new locations to future work (p. 15). The antenna configuration is not stated. The first page holds the title and the DOI matches (p. 1).
